title: Temporal: Durable Execution
subtitle: Workflow code coordinates work; event history makes progress recoverable

blocks.title: Core architecture
blocks.diagram:
flowchart LR
  C[Client] --> S[Temporal service]
  S --> Q[Task queue]
  Q --> W[Worker]
  W -->|Commands| S
  W -->|Schedule| A[Activity]
  A -->|Result or failure| S

blocks.title: Workflow task and activity
blocks.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant Service as Temporal service
  participant Worker
  participant Activity
  Client->>Service: Start
  Service->>Worker: History + task
  Worker->>Service: Schedule activity
  Service->>Activity: Execute
  Activity-->>Service: Result or failure
  Service->>Worker: Updated history
  Worker->>Service: Complete
  Service-->>Client: Result

blocks.title: Retries belong at the activity boundary
blocks.text: A failed activity can be retried according to its retry policy. Workflow code replays its recorded history to rebuild state, so workflow logic must be deterministic; external side effects belong in activities.

blocks.title: Why execution survives worker loss
blocks.text: Workers are replaceable executors. The service persists workflow events, then gives the history to a worker when a workflow task is dispatched. A restarted worker can replay those events and continue from the resulting state without relying on its former process memory.

blocks.label: durable event history
blocks.detail: Recorded events let another worker replay and continue the workflow.
